title: ‘हारजित’  कथामा सांस्कृतिक प्रभुत्व
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेखमा भवानी भिक्षुद्वारा लिखित ‘हारजित’  कथालाई प्रभुत्व (हेजेमोनी) सम्बन्धी सिद्घान्तका दृष्टिले विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । सदियौंदेखि इतिहासमा समावेश भएका वा बनाइएका समाजका वा राज्यका नेतृत्वदायीतहमा रहेर आफ्नो आवाजलाई प्रभुत्वशाली बनाएका व्यक्ति वा समूदाय नै प्रभुत्वशाली हुन् । हेजेमोनी एउटा बृहत् सिद्घान्त हो । विचार धारात्मकरूपले हेर्दा यसमा एकभन्दा बढी विचारको बहुलता देखिन्छ । यसभित्र प्रभुत्वशाली वर्गको प्रभुत्वको अवस्था, प्रभुत्व हासिल गर्ने शैली र प्रतिप्रभुत्वको अवस्था पहिचान गरी समाजमा उनीहरूको स्थान, प्रभुत्व र प्रतिरोधको अवस्थाको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यस कथाको समाजमा वर्गीय दृष्टिले उच्च वर्गको, जातीय दृष्टिले उच्च जातिको वा उच्च संस्कृतिको समुदायका जातिको र लैङ्गिक दृष्टिले पुरूषको प्रभुत्व रहेको देखिन्छ भने प्रतिरोधको भावना सशक्त देखिँदैन । प्रस्तुत लेखमा प्रभुत्वशाली वर्गहरूमा हामीले जतिसुकै शोषण गरेपनि उनीहरू हाम्रा विरुद्ध बोल्न सक्दैनन् र बोलीहाले भनेपनि उनीहरूको केही सीप लाग्दैन भन्ने हैकमवादी प्रभुत्व र गरिबवर्गहरूमा कतिपय नमिल्दा कुराहरूमा आवाज उठाउन पछि पर्नुहुन्न भन्ने जागरुक दृष्टिकोण रहेको निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: The presented article examined the story ‘Harjit’, written by Bhavani Bhakshyudara, from the standpoint of cultural hegemony (Hegemony) as a related theory. Ever since ancient times, those who lived in societies or states that were part of or came into being in history, and made themselves hegemonic by raising their voices, have themselves been hegemonic. Hegemony is a broad theory. When viewed from a theoretical perspective, more than one idea is revealed in it. Within the study, after identifying the condition of hegemony of the hegemonic class, the style of attaining hegemony, and the state of reciprocal hegemony, the position, hegemony and resistance of the society were analyzed. In the society of this story, a high caste is seen from a class perspective, a high-caste member of a community with a high ethnicity or high culture is seen from an ethnic perspective, and male dominance is seen from a gender perspective, while the sense of resistance is not strong. In the presented article, even if we exploit the hegemonic classes however much, they cannot speak against us, and even if they do speak, they do not have such ability; therefore, a conclusion of a cautious approach to raising voices was drawn.

australian_english: The presented article took a squiz at the story ‘Harjit’ penned by Bhavani Bhakshyudara, looking at it through the lens of cultural hegemony (Hegemony) as a related theory. Going back a long way, ever since ancient times, those who lived in societies or states that were part of or came into being in history and made themselves hegemonic by raising their voices have themselves been hegemonic. Hegemony is a pretty broad theory. When you look at it through a theoretical lens, you see heaps more than one idea in it. Within the research, once they’d identified the state of hegemony of the hegemonic class, the way they got to be hegemonic, and the state of reciprocal hegemony, they went and analysed the society’s position, hegemony and resistance. In the society of this story, a high caste is seen from a class angle, a high-caste member of a community with a high ethnic background or high culture is seen from an ethnic angle, and male dominance is seen from a gender angle, but the resistance doesn’t seem to be all that strong. In the presented article, even if we gave it a burl and exploited the hegemonic classes no matter how much, they couldn’t say a word against us, and even if they did, they didn’t have the nous for it; so a conclusion of a cautious approach to raising voices was drawn.
informal_english: So the article here goes and has a gander at the story ‘Harjit’ written by Bhavani Bhakshyudara, and checks out the whole cultural hegemony (Hegemony) theory. Going way back, ever since ancient times, if you had a society or a state that was in the mix or got going in history and made their voices heard to be hegemonic, then they were the hegemon. And the whole thing is a big theory, eh. If you squint through a theoretical lens, you can see heaps of ideas in it. And in the research they figured out the state of the hegemonic class, how they pulled the strings, and the reciprocal state, then they went and analysed the society’s position, the hegemony and the resistance. In the society of that story, from a class point of view you see a high caste, from an ethnic point of view a high-caste bloke from a community with a high ethnic background or high culture, and from a gender point of view you see male dominance; but the resistance didn’t seem all that strong. In the article here, even if we exploited those hegemonic blokes as much as we liked, they couldn’t say boo to us, and even if they did talk, they didn’t have the skills; so they came to a conclusion about being careful with raising voices.
